newsitem.title: USA: US Plains fed cattle bid $68, passed - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: US Plains fed cattle bid $68, passed - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle bids at $68.00 per cwt were light and passed by owners pricing cattle at $70.00, feedlot sources said.

The bulk of last week's active cattle sales were at $69.00. Trade this week have a "50-50" chance of reaching $70.00, depending on beef demand and the number of cattle on this week's showlists, several cattle feeders said.
This week's showlists reportedly were about unchanged to smaller than last week, with aggressive marketing of cattle the past three weeks keeping feedlots extremely current, sources said.
Support from tight market-ready cattle supplies could be offset by ideas that beef demand was waning following active retailer buying ahead of Memorial Day holiday beef promotions.
Beef sales last week was estimated at 1,222 loads, down 8.1 percent from the previous week's tally at 1,330, USDA statistics showed.
The average price for heavyweight choice beef ended the week at $106.97 per cwt, up $0.74 from the previous Friday. However, the price fell $1.61 the last three days of the week.
Beef prices at midday Monday were quoted down $0.03 to $0.12, on 57 loads sold, USDA said.
Heavier-weight choice beef prices slipped $0.08 to $106.89.
